sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Purpose and prompt rules for workforce
sections.what: Explains that this agent describes which roles change, in which direction, and what skills they need. The prompt tells the model never to give numbers for people or money.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: a number here would be a total produced by an agent, and it would look authoritative next to a role name.
sections.watch_out: The prompt rule and the output shape both block numbers, so loosening either one lets quantities through.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Pattern check for numbers in text
sections.what: Defines a list of countable nouns and a pattern that detects percentages, currency amounts and counts of people written in free text. It is meant to catch numbers that slip into descriptions.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: the output shape cannot see free text, so this is a backstop. It is kept conservative so labels like tier 2 support still pass.
sections.watch_out: A broader pattern would block legitimate labels and push people to work around the check.

sections.name: _WorkforceOutput
sections.title: Shape of the workforce answer
sections.what: Defines the answer shape: operating model changes, one entry per affected role, and a list of evidence IDs. Each role entry has a direction and skills, with no field for a headcount or a money amount.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: the missing number field is the enforcement. A request not to quantify would be weaker.
sections.watch_out: Adding any numeric field here would remove the main protection against invented headcount figures.

sections.name: WorkforceModeller
sections.title: Workforce agent and number check
sections.what: The agent that sends the redesigned process to the model, then scans the free-text fields for numbers. If it finds one, it stops with an error rather than passing it on.
sections.why: Likely reason: released effort is calculated elsewhere, where the cost of an FTE is known, so a number here would be an unchecked total.
sections.watch_out: A false match in this check raises an error that can stop a valid run, so a broad pattern would cause real failures.

summary: Asks an AI model to describe the workforce and operating model effects of a redesign as directions and skills only, and rejects numbers that appear in free text.
purpose: Describes the people side of a redesign: which roles change, in which direction, and what skills they need. It contains no money or headcount figures.
why: Released effort and cost are calculated in the value package, which knows what a full-time role costs. Keeping numbers out of this stage avoids unchecked totals.
how: Build a prompt from the purpose, posture and redesigned steps. The model returns operating model changes, role directions and skills, plus evidence IDs. Free-text fields are scanned for numbers. If none are found, the implications object is built and returned.
inputs: The future state: its purpose, posture and redesigned steps, including who performs each step.
outputs: An implications object with operating model items, workforce items and evidence IDs.
risks: A number written in a form the pattern does not match will pass through. A false match blocks a valid run. Directions chosen by the model may be too optimistic about reductions.
debug: If the run fails with a quantification error, the message lists the matched text. Check whether those are real quantities or labels. If role directions look wrong, check the steps passed in.
